arenson9:
@VisforYoshi I've never played any game on a gaming console. We have a Wii, purchased entirely so we could try out (and later abandon) Wii Fit. I like cooperative, turn-based strategy games.  What would you recommend?

 

Well, I don't typically play multiplaeter games, so I'm not the best to ask for multiplayer games. However in terms of single player games, I can name a few (and I'm going off of the regular Wii, not the Wii U):

 

Pikmin 1 and 2 (new play control): Considered an RTS, it's fun if you're good at it and still fun if you're terrible (I enjoy it, and I'm really bad). Not the best game to play for a couple of minutes and do something else due to the day/night mechanic, but if you like RTS-style games, it's worth looking into

 

Kirby's Return to Dreamland: Kirby is an easy game to pick up and play, and this game does have a co-op play for up to 4 players. And since Kirby is fairly consistant, if you've played another Kirby game and liked it, you'll like this one. It's actually my personal favorite in the series

 

Donkey Kong Country Returns: Skip New Super Mario Bros Wii. If you want a fun co-op platformer, go with Return to Dreamland If you want a great single player one (with some difficulty to it), go with this one. The level design is phenominal (assuming you like sidescrollers)

 

Xenoblade Chronicles: Depending on where you live, the Wii version may be pretty hard to get… so if you have a New 3DS or a Wii U, get it on that instead, it will save some money (and updated resolutions, because the graphics on the original wii one is kind of… dated looking in terms of resolution. But still very pretty, artistically speaking). This is a game that feels like a hybrid between a JRPG and a Western RPG. It feels like a single player MMO, with a battlesystem that have attacks with cooldown timers and a wide world to explore. The story alone took me over 70 hours to complete, so you'll get quite a bit of playtime out of this one

 

Super Mario Galaxy (1, not 2): The best 3D platformer I've played, hands down. If you liked Mario 64, chances are you'll like this one. It has a 2 player mode that's… a bit underwhelming to the player 2, but still a fun game.

 

Super Paper Mario: This one is different from the previous 2 Paper Mario games, but still good. The best story of the three, this game is primarily a puzzle based platformer/sidescroller. It's a creative game with a good story (from a Mario standpoint), but the extra content in it (namley the pit of 100 trials) leaves something to be desired… it's a bit poorly designed

 

Kirby's Epic Yarn: As dumb as the name is, it's a really good game. Even though Kirby can't use his iconic eating of things, it's a lot of fun to play. Th visuals are creative, the music is comforting, and it's one of the best pick-me-up games out there. I have never ended a play session of this game in a bad mood.

 

Metroid Prime Trilogy: From what I hear, this one is a bit harder to find (although, Metroid Prime 3 is on the Wii, and doesn't really require any knowledge of 1 and 2 to play), but it contains the games to an interesting series. The optional lore adds a lot of life into the worlds, the music is good, and the gameplay is pretty fun. Sometimes the bosses are pretty brutal, but not impossible. I've had to take a few tries to beat some of the bosses and areas.

 

I'm sure I'm missing a few, but those are some great single player Wii games that I can remember (Yeah, I like platformers a lot). For multiplayer, the best I can give you is Smash Bros and Mario Kart, but even then I don't really care for either of them that much (I never get any use out of my multiplayer games).

Ario:

@rabit: What was the last truly excellent art experience you had?

Wow. Art is such a broad topic, and I’m lucky enough to enjoy a great deal of it:

  • An amazingly faithful representation of Spiderman in [i]Civil War[/i]
  • The excellent van Gogh exhibit at the Chicago Art Institute we were able to visit a couple months ago
  • The wonderous universes we cooperatively create and evolve in our bi-weekly tabletop sessions (which is art, I've learned)
  • Finally seeing [i]The Chorus Line[/i] off-Broadway, after years of loving and feeling a connection to the music and story
  • My astonishment at the decades of material I’ve accumulated from GMing my home-brewed RPG campaign world

But honestly, “the last truly excellent art experience” I’ve had was the gift my spouse made for me for a recent anniversary (just a couple weeks ago), a book that wonderfully explained our relationship in a way that brought us both to tears as I read it.

 

Nielzabub:

@ Rabit: How do you deal with your natural predators? Do you run, fight, convince them to just chill out and game with your, or some other option?

As with so many things, it depends on the situation – and the threat.

For most threats, I’ll start by approaching it in a manner opposite to the threat. (For example, smile at the predator and try to find things we’re both interested in.) In situations where that doesn’t work – or where I know going in it won’t work – I’ll do a quick cost-benefit analysis on the situation to determine if fighting or fleeing are the better option. If others are at threat, I’ll pretty much fight every time, though.

Sometimes I can get lucky and determine there’s a bigger predator I can lure over to distract (or otherwise deal with) the threat, but I’ll usually avoid that approach unless it’s absolutely necessary. I’d rather not attract too much of the bigger predator’s attention – and I prefer to remain low profile, in general.

 

(Check out the recent Invisibilia podcast’s “Flip the Script” for thoughts on approaching hostility with kindness. )

bobbertoriley:

@Rabit - What is your zombie survival plan?

 

Nothing complex, really…

Our (new to us) house is decently defensible, given a couple modifications (like boarding up a few ground-floor windows). The back is mostly fenced in, with just one section open (which we’ll likely address very soon).

Melee weapons aren’t a problem; I have a decent collection here. I’ve already found the place I’ll go for a bow, arrows, and appropriate supplies (repair materials, etc.) to go with them, now that I have the room. But that’s mainly for food hunting and scaring off looters, as zombies will go down to a sling much easier than a bow. Sling stones do more appropriate damage for taking out zombies.

I’m not a proponent of guns as part of a zombie survival plan. Too many issues and risks, including not being able to get or make ammo (that won’t blow up in your own face). Slings can use anything small and heavy. And arrows can be made, with the right skill.

In the initial insanity, looting will include the local drug stores just a couple blocks away, both the CVS and Walgreens. That stash of medicine will be worth more than just about anything when it comes time to start trading. They also have a decent amount of food that can be used in the short term until we can get to self-sufficiency.

I’ll be able to pull out my (annually-refreshed) emergency seed supply to start gardening in our back yard. The garage will be converted into pens for chickens, rabbits, and a horse or two. (One of the first things we’ll do is raid the local carriage company’s stables just a couple blocks away.)

The house is very close to the canal, which has a natural flow of water – when the water company falls to the hordes, we’ll still have water nearby we can use, although it’ll likely need to be decontaminated.

Depending on how our neighbors fair, we might be able to annex one of their yards. Both are well fenced in, allowing us some great potential garden space.

 

Mind you, some of these details are only true in the alternate universe where zombies exist and I’m single without any responsibilities that would preclude me doing some of these things.

I’ll let you decided which details are true…

That's a hard call! I haven't actually made any co-op games yet, so that avenue is out. My favourite game that I've made is Dracula's Feast - the puzzley elements make me think SotM fans might enjoy that, and the modular nature of it is directly inspired by Sentinels.

My second call would be Hex Mex, because I codesigned that with Christopher and so obviously there's a lot of his design sensibilities in it. It's hugely thematic, fun, and it has a co-op mode that I could see people really getting into!
